previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and a history of kidney and pancreas transplants was admitted with sepsis and right leg cellulitis. She presented with high fever, chills, and hypotension requiring ICU admission. Blood cultures eventually grew Enterococcus, likely originating from the cellulitis. She was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to vancomycin delivered via peritoneal dialysis after removal of her tunneled dialysis catheter. She developed oral and presumed esophageal candidiasis, treated with fluconazole, which required tacrolimus dose adjustment. Her anemia was managed with two units of packed red blood cells. She had transient transaminitis and elevated CK, attributed to daptomycin, which was discontinued. Her anticoagulation was held and restarted at a low dose, with INR remaining subtherapeutic at discharge. She improved clinically, with resolving infection and stable cardiac function, and was discharged to extended care with a two-week course of outpatient antibiotics and close follow-up.

seen beneath the diaphragm.

No obvious displaced rib fractures are seen.  If there is a high clinical
concern for a nondisplaced rib fracture, dedicated rib series scan be
